audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Deuteronomy / Devarim flogging, working-animal, levirate, mutilation, weights, and Amalek law, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for judicial flogging limit, human dignity, unmuzzled ox, levirate marriage and refusal ritual, woman's hand-cutting penalty, honest measures, and Amalek memory command.

verses.restored: If there is dispute between men and they approach judgment, and judges judge them, they shall justify righteous one and condemn wicked one.

familiar.text: If there be a controversy between men, and they come unto judgment, that the judges may judge them; then they shall justify the righteous, and condemn the wicked.

modern.text: If there is a dispute between men, they are to go to court to be judged, so that the innocent may be acquitted and the guilty condemned.

original.text: כִּֽי יִהְיֶ֥ה רִיב֙ בֵּ֣ין אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְנִגְּשׁ֥וּ אֶל הַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט וּשְׁפָט֑וּם וְהִצְדִּ֨יקוּ֙ אֶת הַצַּדִּ֔יק וְהִרְשִׁ֖יעוּ אֶת הָרָשָֽׁע

verses.restored: It shall be, if wicked one deserves striking, judge shall cause him to lie down and he shall be struck before him according to measure of his wickedness, by number.

familiar.text: And it shall be, if the wicked man be worthy to be beaten, that the judge shall cause him to lie down, and to be beaten before his face, according to his fault, by a certain number.

modern.text: If the guilty man deserves to be beaten, the judge shall have him lie down and be flogged in his presence with the number of lashes his crime warrants.

original.text: וְהָיָ֛ה אִם בִּ֥ן הַכּ֖וֹת הָרָשָׁ֑ע וְהִפִּיל֤וֹ הַשֹּׁפֵט֙ וְהִכָּ֣הוּ לְפָנָ֔יו כְּדֵ֥י רִשְׁעָת֖וֹ בְּמִסְפָּֽר

verses.restored: Forty he may strike him, he shall not add, lest if he adds to strike him beyond these with many blows, your brother be degraded in your eyes.

familiar.text: Forty stripes he may give him, and not exceed: lest, if he should exceed, and beat him above these with many stripes, then thy brother should seem vile unto thee.

modern.text: He may receive no more than forty lashes, lest your brother be beaten any more than that and be degraded in your sight.

original.text: אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יַכֶּ֖נּוּ לֹ֣א יֹסִ֑יף פֶּן יֹסִ֨יף לְהַכֹּת֤וֹ עַל אֵ֨לֶּה֙ מַכָּ֣ה רַבָּ֔ה וְנִקְלָ֥ה אָחִ֖יךָ לְעֵינֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: You shall not muzzle ox while it threshes.

familiar.text: Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn.

modern.text: Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain. Widowhood and Marriage

verses.restored: If brothers dwell together and one of them dies and has no son, wife of dead shall not become wife outside to a strange man; her brother-in-law shall go in to her and take her to himself as wife and perform brother-in-law duty to her.

familiar.text: If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband’s brother unto her.

modern.text: When brothers dwell together and one of them dies without a son, the widow must not marry outside the family. Her husband’s brother is to take her as his wife and fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law for her.

familiar.text: And it shall be, that the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.

modern.text: The first son she bears will carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name will not be blotted out from Israel.

translation_notes: The maximum of forty lashes limits corporal punishment and explicitly protects the condemned person's status as brother, but modern justice should not reenact judicial flogging.
The unmuzzled-ox law recognizes that a working animal may eat from the labor it performs and supports broader labor and animal-welfare ethics.
Levirate marriage seeks lineage and economic continuity for a widow, but the woman's future and reproductive labor remain constrained by patriarchal kinship expectations.
The refusal ritual gives the widow a public voice and allows the man to decline, though at the cost of shame.

The hand-cutting penalty in verses 11-12 is a gendered mutilation law focused on male reproductive injury. It must never be enforced and must not override a person's right to defend another from violence.
Honest weights and measures make ordinary commerce a matter of justice before YHWH.
The Amalek command turns memory of an attack on exhausted stragglers into a mandate to erase a people. It must never be mapped onto any modern ethnic, national, religious, or political group.
safety_note: Do not use Deuteronomy 25 to justify flogging, mutilation, coerced marriage, reproductive control, public sexual humiliation, or genocide in the name of Amalek. Center limits on punishment, dignity even for the condemned, animal and worker welfare, public recourse for widows, and honest commerce.
